doc.calendar_a11y_desc: Uses role='grid' with proper aria-label. Date cells are navigable with arrow keys. Selected date is announced with aria-selected.
doc.calendar_anatomy_content: The grid displaying days of the month, sorted by week.
doc.calendar_anatomy_root: The primary wrapper that handles date calculations, month/year navigation, and state management.
doc.calendar_best_practice_1: Use Calendar consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.calendar_best_practice_2: Test Calendar behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.calendar_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like DatePicker better suits the use case.
doc.calendar_choice_self_when: When Calendar functionality with standard options is required.
doc.calendar_design_intent: Calendar provides a standalone date selection interface, allowing users to view and pick dates from a monthly grid without a text input field.
doc.calendar_scenario_1: Event Dashboards: Displaying a monthly overview of scheduled meetings or deadlines.
doc.calendar_scenario_2: Booking Systems: Selecting a check-in date for a hotel or resource reservation.
doc.colorinput_a11y_desc: The colour swatch is given a translated accessible name but is tabIndex -1, so it does not add a second tab stop next to the field it belongs to. The text input remains the control: it is what receives focus, what carries the field's name and validation wiring, and what a screen reader reads the value from. Because the swatch conveys the current colour visually and nothing else, the value has to remain readable as text in the input.
doc.colorinput_anatomy_content: The text field for entering precise color values (Hex, RGB, etc.).
doc.colorinput_anatomy_root: The container that harmonizes the text input with a live color swatch preview.
doc.colorinput_best_practice_1: Use ColorInput consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.colorinput_best_practice_2: Test ColorInput behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.colorinput_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like ColorPicker better suits the use case.
doc.colorinput_choice_self_when: When ColorInput functionality with standard options is required.
doc.colorinput_design_intent: ColorInput allows users to enter exact color values via text while providing a live preview. It is ideal for design settings or theme configurations where precise hex or RGB codes are necessary.
doc.colorinput_long_desc: A component that provides a color input.
doc.colorinput_scenario_1: Brand Settings: Allowing admins to specify exact primary colors for their white-label app.
doc.colorinput_scenario_2: CSS Editors: Providing a way to enter and preview hex codes in a developer-focused tool.
doc.colorinput_title: Field for selecting colors and entering hex codes with preview
doc.colorpicker_a11y_desc: This is a thin wrapper around Input: it adds layout and styling and no ARIA of its own, so the roles, the accessible name and the keyboard behaviour all come from Input. Read that component's accessibility notes — anything required there is required here, and props you pass through reach it unchanged.
doc.colorpicker_anatomy_content: The visual palette or spectrum where users can interactively select a color.
doc.colorpicker_anatomy_root: The trigger or container that manages the picker's visibility and current selection state.
doc.colorpicker_best_practice_1: Use ColorPicker consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.colorpicker_best_practice_2: Test ColorPicker behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.colorpicker_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like ColorInput better suits the use case.
doc.colorpicker_choice_self_when: When ColorPicker functionality with standard options is required.
doc.colorpicker_design_intent: ColorPicker provides a visual interface for selecting colors from a spectrum. It is intended for scenarios where users need to creatively explore and 'find' a color rather than entering a known value.
doc.colorpicker_long_desc: A component for users to pick colors. It wraps the native input type="color" and adjusts its styles.
doc.colorpicker_scenario_1: Design Tools: Picking a custom background color for a presentation slide.
doc.colorpicker_scenario_2: User Personalization: Letting users choose a highlight color for their dashboard theme.
doc.colorpicker_title: Component for choosing colors from a visual palette
doc.datepicker_a11y_2: `aria-label` or `aria-describedby` is set for the input field.
doc.datepicker_a11y_4: Disabled dates are explicitly marked with aria-disabled.
doc.datepicker_a11y_desc: The calendar popup uses role='dialog' with aria-label. Date cells are navigable with arrow keys. Selected date is announced with aria-selected.
doc.datepicker_a11y_keyboard: Navigate through dates in the calendar with arrow keys and make selection possible with the Enter key. Also, allow closing the calendar with the Escape key.
doc.datepicker_adv_1: Intuitive date entry without needing specific calendar knowledge.
doc.datepicker_adv_2: Visual confirmation of dates via the calendar UI.
doc.datepicker_adv_3: Automatically prevents format errors during entry.
doc.datepicker_adv_4: Full support for accessible keyboard navigation.
doc.datepicker_anatomy_input: A field that displays the currently selected date and accepts keyboard input.
doc.datepicker_anatomy_popup: A floating panel for visually listing and selecting dates.
doc.datepicker_best_practice_1: Use clear date format labels (e.g., 'MM/DD/YYYY') so users know the expected input format.
doc.datepicker_best_practice_2: Provide both keyboard input and calendar picker to accommodate different user preferences.
doc.datepicker_choice_input_when: When entering a date the user already remembers quickly (e.g., date of birth, expiration date).
doc.datepicker_choice_matrix_desc: Select the optimal entry method depending on the nature of the date to be entered.
doc.datepicker_choice_picker_when: When it's necessary to select while checking the day of the week or availability (e.g., reservation date, event date).
doc.datepicker_clear_btn_desc: Optionally display a button to instantly clear the selected date.
doc.datepicker_content_format: Display the appropriate date format (YYYY/MM/DD, etc.) for the user's locale and communicate entry examples through placeholders.
doc.datepicker_control_types_desc: DatePicker supports both controlled and uncontrolled patterns.
doc.datepicker_custom_format_desc: Control the display format in the input field using the format property.
doc.datepicker_custom_popup_desc: Customize the content of the calendar popup using available slots.
doc.datepicker_design_intent: DatePicker is a component designed to allow users to intuitively select dates through a calendar-format UI. By being able to see the sense of the day of the week and specific periods (yesterday, tomorrow, etc.) while selecting, it prevents entry errors and reduces the user's memory load.
doc.datepicker_flow_1: Click the first time to select the start date.
doc.datepicker_flow_2: Click the second time to select the end date.
doc.datepicker_flow_3: The range between the start and end dates is highlighted during selection.
doc.datepicker_flow_4: If a date earlier than the start date is selected as the end date, they are automatically swapped.
doc.datepicker_guideline_1: Use when users need to select a specific date or ranges with visual calendar confirmation.
doc.datepicker_guideline_2: For dates users know by heart (e.g., birth dates, expiry dates), direct text input is often more efficient.
doc.datepicker_integration_desc: DatePicker utilizes the shared Calendar component internally. See the Calendar documentation for more details.
doc.datepicker_kb_1: Press Enter or Space on the input field to open the calendar.
doc.datepicker_kb_2: Navigate through dates with arrow keys and press Enter to select.
doc.datepicker_kb_3: Close the calendar anytime by pressing the Escape key.
doc.datepicker_long_desc: Details and usage for the Date Picker component.
doc.datepicker_ts_desc: The DatePicker component provides comprehensive type definitions for safe usage.
doc.daterangepicker_a11y_desc: Both start and end date inputs are keyboard-accessible. The calendar popup announces the selected range via aria-live updates.
doc.daterangepicker_best_practice_1: Show a visual preview of the selected range between start and end dates in the calendar.
doc.daterangepicker_best_practice_2: Validate that the end date is not before the start date and provide clear error feedback.
doc.daterangepicker_choice_alt_when: When only a single date is needed (use DatePicker instead).
doc.daterangepicker_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the type of date selection needed.
doc.daterangepicker_choice_self_when: When users need to select a start and end date as a range (e.g., booking dates, report periods).
doc.daterangepicker_long_desc: Detailed information and usage instructions for the daterangepicker component.
doc.daterangepicker_title: A component for selecting a specific date range (start and end dates).
doc.inputmask_a11y_desc: This is a thin wrapper around Input: it adds layout and styling and no ARIA of its own, so the roles, the accessible name and the keyboard behaviour all come from Input. Read that component's accessibility notes — anything required there is required here, and props you pass through reach it unchanged.
doc.inputmask_anatomy_content: The text field that dynamically formats the content as the user types.
doc.inputmask_anatomy_root: The container that manages the masking logic and ensures the input follows the defined pattern.
doc.inputmask_basic_desc: Specify a pattern in the mask property.
doc.inputmask_best_practice_1: Use InputMask consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.inputmask_best_practice_2: Test InputMask behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.inputmask_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Input better suits the use case.
doc.inputmask_choice_self_when: When InputMask functionality with standard options is required.
doc.inputmask_design_intent: InputMask enforces a specific character format (such as phone numbers, CCs, or dates) during entry, reducing user error and ensuring high data quality without manual formatting.
doc.inputmask_long_desc: An input component with a mask to enforce input following a specific format.
doc.inputmask_scenario_1: Financial Entry: Enforcing a 16-digit pattern with spaces for credit card numbers.
doc.inputmask_scenario_2: Contact Info: Formatting phone numbers (e.g., (999) 999-9999) as the user types.
doc.numberinput_a11y_stepper: Assign appropriate aria-labels to the spin buttons so their function can be understood by screen readers.
doc.numberinput_anatomy_input: An <input> element that accepts only numerical values.
doc.numberinput_anatomy_steppers: Up and down buttons for increasing or decreasing the value by a certain amount.
doc.numberinput_best_practice_1: Always define min, max, and step to prevent invalid out-of-range values and to convey the expected input range to the user.
doc.numberinput_best_practice_2: Display a unit label (e.g., 'kg', '%', '$') adjacent to the field so users understand the expected value format without guessing.
doc.numberinput_choice_matrix_desc: Select according to the nature of the value to be entered and the frequency of adjustment.
doc.numberinput_choice_number_when: When continuous increment/decrement operations of numerical values such as quantity, age, or price are expected.
doc.numberinput_choice_slider_when: When intuitive proportions or sensory adjustments within a range are prioritized over precise numerical values.
doc.numberinput_choice_text_when: For 'numbers' with a strong symbolic meaning, such as phone numbers, credit card numbers, or zip codes (see [Numeric Input Standardization](./?path=/docs/standardization-numeric-input-standardization--docs)).
doc.numberinput_design_intent: NumberInput is a component specialized for entering and fine-tuning numerical values. In addition to users directly entering numbers using the keyboard, it provides a UI where values can be intuitively adjusted using spin buttons (increment/decrement buttons).
doc.numberinput_long_desc: A component that provides numerical input.
doc.numberinput_scenario_admin: Admin Panel: Specifying the sort order (priority) numerically.
doc.numberinput_scenario_cart: Shopping Cart: Changing the number of items ordered (quantity).
doc.numberinput_title: Field specialized for numeric input with spin buttons
doc.otpinput_a11y_desc: Each digit input is individually focusable with auto-advance. Supports paste for the full code. Uses aria-label to describe the purpose.
doc.otpinput_a11y_label: Communicate to screen readers that each field is requesting individual entry, and make them recognize it as an 'authentication code entry' as a whole group.
doc.otpinput_anatomy_fields: Input Field Sequence: A group of inputs dedicated to a single character, lined up for the specified number of digits.
doc.otpinput_best_practice_1: Auto-focus the first input field when the OTP screen loads to reduce friction.
doc.otpinput_best_practice_2: Support pasting the entire OTP code from clipboard to improve the user experience.
doc.otpinput_choice_alt_when: When the input is a general text field without specific digit-by-digit entry (use Input).
doc.otpinput_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the type of code input needed.
doc.otpinput_choice_self_when: When verifying identity with a one-time passcode (SMS, email, or authenticator app).
doc.otpinput_content_auto: To enhance convenience on mobile devices, it supports automatic completion from SMS (autocomplete="one-time-code").
doc.otpinput_design_intent: OtpInput is a specialized component for entering short authentication codes (usually 4 to 6 digits) used in two-factor authentication, etc. By providing fields categorized for each character, it clarifies the current entry position and reduces entry errors by functioning as a visual guide.
doc.segmentedcontrol_a11y_desc: The group is role="radiogroup" named by the visible label through aria-labelledby, with aria-required, aria-invalid and aria-describedby set from the field state. Each option is role="radio" with aria-checked and a roving tabindex, so the group is one tab stop. Arrow keys move to the next or previous option and wrap around at both ends, and because this is a radio group they also change the selection, not just the focus. The sliding indicator behind the options is aria-hidden.
doc.segmentedcontrol_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.segmentedcontrol_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.segmentedcontrol_basic_desc: A set of buttons primarily used to toggle between different views or layout options.
doc.segmentedcontrol_best_practice_1: Use SegmentedControl consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.segmentedcontrol_best_practice_2: Test SegmentedControl behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.segmentedcontrol_compare_desc: For detailed differentiation, refer to the Selection Controls Guide. It summarizes differences between SegmentedControl, Dropdown, Tabs, and Button Group, and provides criteria for choosing between them.
doc.segmentedcontrol_count_desc:
- Recommended: Keep to 2–5 items.
- Reason: To maintain a design where each item has sufficient width and is easy to tap even on mobile screens.
- If there are too many: For 6 or more items, or if labels have many characters (5+), consider the following:
- Dropdown
- Tab bar (scrollable tabs)
doc.segmentedcontrol_count_reason: To maintain a design where each item has sufficient width and is easy to tap even on mobile screens.
doc.segmentedcontrol_count_too_many: For 6 or more items, or if labels have many characters (5+), consider the following:
doc.segmentedcontrol_design_intent: SegmentedControl provides a consistent, reusable pattern for mutually exclusive toggle group for switching data views, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.segmentedcontrol_ex_app_settings: Light Mode / Dark Mode / System Settings
doc.segmentedcontrol_ex_attr: Male / Female / Other, In Stock / All
doc.segmentedcontrol_ex_category: All / Replies / Mentions (notifications), All / Missed Calls (phone app)
doc.segmentedcontrol_ex_time: Day / Week / Month switch in calendar
doc.segmentedcontrol_guideline_desc:
All options must be visible at once.
Do not allow horizontal scrolling, such as when tab triggers do not fit on the screen.
doc.segmentedcontrol_icon_desc: Icons and labels can be used together, or only icons can be displayed.
doc.segmentedcontrol_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the segmented control. Arrow keys navigate between segments. The focused segment is automatically selected.
doc.segmentedcontrol_long_desc: Details and usage for the SegmentedControl component.
doc.segmentedcontrol_opt_desc: Text labels should be concise and clear nouns or noun phrases.
doc.segmentedcontrol_opt_lang_note: Multi-language support: Consider that character counts may change significantly when switching between languages.
doc.segmentedcontrol_p_space_desc: Suitable for limited screen sizes such as smartphones by saving space with icon-only displays.
doc.segmentedcontrol_p_state_desc: Each segment has an Active (selected) and Inactive (unselected) state.
doc.segmentedcontrol_p_struct_desc: Consists of at least two segments.
doc.segmentedcontrol_scenario_1: View Toggling: Switching between 'List', 'Grid', and 'Calendar' layouts in a task manager.
doc.segmentedcontrol_scenario_2: Filtering Options: Quickly refining results by 'Price', 'Popularity', or 'Newest' without a dropdown.
doc.segmentedcontrol_two_desc:
Also available for two choices (e.g., On/Off, Yes/No).
Ensure that the design clearly indicates which one is selected when there are only two choices.
doc.segmentedcontrol_u1_desc: Pattern where the entire page layout or presentation itself changes significantly.
doc.segmentedcontrol_u2_desc: Restricts the "type" of data displayed, serving a role similar to tab menus.
doc.segmentedcontrol_u3_desc: Changes the order of data. Useful for one-tap switching when choices are few enough that a dropdown isn’t necessary.
doc.segmentedcontrol_u4_desc: Determines the "state" for a specific item.
doc.otpinput_length_change_desc: Change the number of input fields with the length property.
doc.otpinput_long_desc: Split input fields for entering one-time passwords (OTP) or PIN codes.
doc.otpinput_scenario_auth: Entering codes during login or password reset.
doc.otpinput_scenario_pay: Entering security codes during high-value payments.
doc.phoneinput_a11y_desc: The country selector is implemented as a native <select> element with aria-label='Country code', ensuring compatibility with assistive technologies. The phone number input uses aria-labelledby to associate itself with the field label, and aria-invalid when an error is present.
doc.phoneinput_anatomy_country: Country Selector: A native select element overlaid on a flag + dial code preview. Allows the user to pick their country.
doc.phoneinput_anatomy_number: Phone Number Input: A tel-type input for entering the local phone number, excluding the country dial code.
doc.phoneinput_best_practice_1: Pre-select the country based on the user's locale or IP geolocation when possible.
doc.phoneinput_best_practice_2: Show a placeholder that matches the expected format for the selected country (e.g., 090-0000-0000 for Japan).
doc.phoneinput_best_practice_3: Validate on submit rather than on every keystroke to avoid frustrating the user during entry.
doc.phoneinput_choice_input_when: When the phone format is always from a single country and no country selection is needed.
doc.phoneinput_choice_inputmask_when: When you need format enforcement (e.g., (99) 9999-9999) without a country selector.
doc.phoneinput_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on whether international phone number entry is required.
doc.phoneinput_choice_phoneinput_when: When users need to enter an international phone number with country code selection.
doc.phoneinput_design_intent: PhoneInput combines a country code selector with a phone number field into a single cohesive input. It solves the common UX problem of collecting international phone numbers by letting users pick their country — displaying the flag and dial code — without needing to manually type the country code.
doc.phoneinput_long_desc: Composite input for international phone numbers with a country dial code selector.
doc.phoneinput_scenario_checkout: E-commerce Checkout: Collecting a shipping contact number that may be from any country.
doc.phoneinput_scenario_signup: User Registration: Collecting a mobile number for SMS verification during international sign-up.
doc.rangecalendar_a11y_desc: This is a thin wrapper around Calendar: it adds layout and styling and no ARIA of its own, so the roles, the accessible name and the keyboard behaviour all come from Calendar. Read that component's accessibility notes — anything required there is required here, and props you pass through reach it unchanged.
doc.rangecalendar_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.rangecalendar_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.rangecalendar_best_practice_1: Use RangeCalendar consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.rangecalendar_best_practice_2: Test RangeCalendar behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.rangecalendar_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like DateRangePicker better suits the use case.
doc.rangecalendar_choice_self_when: When RangeCalendar functionality with standard options is required.
doc.rangecalendar_design_intent: RangeCalendar provides a consistent, reusable pattern for standalone calendar for selecting a date range without text input, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.rangecalendar_scenario_1: Vacation Planning: Selecting a continuous block of dates for a flight and hotel stay.
doc.rangecalendar_scenario_2: Analytics Filtering: Choosing a custom start and end date to filter a performance dashboard.
doc.rangeslider_a11y_desc: Both thumbs are keyboard-navigable with arrow keys. Each thumb has aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-valuenow attributes.
doc.rangeslider_best_practice_1: Display the current min and max values near the thumbs or in adjacent inputs for precise control.
doc.rangeslider_best_practice_2: Prevent thumbs from crossing each other to maintain intuitive min-max semantics.
doc.rangeslider_choice_alt_when: When only a single numeric value is needed (use Slider).
doc.rangeslider_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on whether a range or single value is needed.
doc.rangeslider_choice_self_when: When users need to define a numeric range (e.g., price range, date range).
doc.rangeslider_long_desc: A slider component for selecting a range (start and end).
doc.slider_a11y_desc: The thumb is keyboard-navigable with arrow keys. Uses role='slider' with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-valuenow.
doc.slider_a11y_keyboard: Ensure values can be increased or decreased by fixed amounts using the left/right (up/down) arrow keys.
doc.slider_anatomy_thumb: A circular handle that the user drags to change the value.
doc.slider_anatomy_track: A line indicating the range of value movement. Colors are separated between selected and unselected ranges.
doc.slider_basic_desc: Standard implementation for selecting a single numeric value from a range.
doc.slider_best_practice_1: Display the current value near the thumb or in a tooltip for precise feedback.
doc.slider_best_practice_2: Define appropriate step sizes to balance precision with ease of use.
doc.slider_choice_matrix_desc: Select according to the nature of the value being selected and the operational precision expected by the user.
doc.slider_choice_number_when: When you want to specify a concrete numerical value precisely in single units, such as age or quantity.
doc.slider_choice_slider_when: When sensory adjustment is more suitable than strict numerical values, such as volume, brightness, or price range.
doc.slider_content_labels: Display labels for the minimum and maximum values to clarify what is being adjusted.
doc.slider_desc: An input to capture a numeric value from a specified range by dragging a knob
doc.slider_design_intent: Sliders are components for selecting a numerical value between a minimum and maximum value through intuitive drag operations. They are ideal when 'relative position' within a range or 'sensory adjustment' is prioritized over precise numerical input.
doc.slider_long_desc: Details and usage for the Slider component.
doc.slider_scenario_filter: Narrowing down a specific price range from a product list.
doc.slider_step_desc: Restrict the numeric increment (step size) using the `step` property.
doc.slider_title: Input to capture a numeric value from a specified range by dragging a knob
doc.slider_usage_desc: Select a numeric value intuitively from the set range by dragging the knob.
doc.timepicker_a11y_desc: This is a thin wrapper around Input: it adds layout and styling and no ARIA of its own, so the roles, the accessible name and the keyboard behaviour all come from Input. Read that component's accessibility notes — anything required there is required here, and props you pass through reach it unchanged.
doc.timepicker_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.timepicker_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.timepicker_best_practice_1: Use TimePicker consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.timepicker_best_practice_2: Test TimePicker behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.timepicker_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like DatePicker better suits the use case.
doc.timepicker_choice_self_when: When TimePicker functionality with standard options is required.
doc.timepicker_desc: A component for users to select time. It wraps the native <input type="time"> and adjusts the styling.
doc.timepicker_design_intent: TimePicker provides a consistent, reusable pattern for time selection input with hour and minute controls, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.timepicker_scenario_1: Shift Management: Setting the start and end times for employee work shifts.
doc.timepicker_scenario_2: Alarms & Reminders: Choosing a specific trigger time for system notifications.
doc.timepicker_title: A specialized input for selecting specific hours and minutes
doc.daterangepicker_scenario_booking: Selecting check-in/check-out dates or reservation periods.
doc.daterangepicker_scenario_report: Defining report date ranges for analytics or data exports.
doc.colorinput_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the color input field. Standard keyboard input is supported for hex values. Escape cancels editing.
doc.colorpicker_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus within the color picker. Arrow keys adjust hue and saturation values. Escape closes the picker.
doc.datepicker_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the date input field. Arrow keys navigate the calendar. Enter selects a date. Escape closes the calendar.
doc.daterangepicker_keyboard_desc: Tab moves between start and end date fields. Arrow keys navigate the calendar. Enter selects dates. Escape closes the calendar.
doc.inputmask_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the masked input field. Standard keyboard input is supported within the mask pattern. Escape cancels where applicable.
doc.rangeslider_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses each slider thumb. Arrow keys adjust the value. Home and End move to min and max values respectively.
doc.slider_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the slider thumb. Arrow keys adjust the value incrementally. Home and End move to min and max values.
doc.timepicker_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the time input field. Arrow keys adjust hours and minutes. Escape closes the time picker panel.
doc.numberinput_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the input. Arrow Up increments the value; Arrow Down decrements it. Home moves to the minimum value; End moves to the maximum. Standard keyboard input is also supported.
doc.otpinput_keyboard_desc: Each digit field is individually focusable. Tab moves between fields. After entering a digit, focus advances automatically to the next field. Backspace clears the current field and moves focus back.
doc.phoneinput_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the country code selector first, then the phone number input. Arrow keys navigate country options in the dropdown. Standard keyboard input is supported in the number field.
